doc.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025

chapter: Time, Creative Music Studio and drumming
title: Berger's rhythm exercises and discipline in free playing
summary: They discuss Berger's GaMaLaTaki syllable exercises and the discipline behind free playing.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: He said an interesting thing that, he said, “Playing free requires more discipline, more stringent than anybody can tell me from the outside. The more precise you get, the more free you are.” And I remember when he said that I just like — wow — that if you observe it and listen to it you may get the impression that people are just playing randomly and that’s not what he’s about at all.

Oh. Yeah, no he had some discipline, he had some exercises that you do, like something called GaMaLaTaki you know GaMaLaTaki GaMaLaTaki Taki Taki Taki Taki GaMaLaTaki Gamala you know. So it breaks up the time. And then doing that, mixing it up is like what do you call that, code for computer which is ones and zeroes. But they’re broken up in different ways. And so then, that’s what he means, it’s discipline of counting and making permutations with those sounds and it gives the player an opportunity to focus more on what they’re doing in improvisation, you know for that kind of direction in learning music.
Would he have people work with that rhythm and those consonants and syllables with just one pitch? Like to play just one pitch on those things to sort of get into it?
Well it wasn’t a pitch, you know you just said it wherever they came out. Yeah. It’s about rhythm. More about rhythm than pitch.

I wish I had gone. He described a roomful of musicians all playing at the same time and fine tuning it with the notes you picked and finding the balance. It just sounded like a really interesting experiment. There’s no question there, but I guess he moved the music forward for sure.
Oh yeah he made a contribution for sure.
